source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use a new sterile needle and syringe for every entry into the vial, and dedicate the multidose vial to one patient whenever possible in clinical practice.","B":"Reuse the same needle for repeated vial entries if a new syringe is attached each time, because the needle does not need replacement until visibly soiled.","C":"Use one syringe for several patients if the needle is changed before each vial entry, because needle replacement prevents contamination of the syringe.","D":"Keep a shared multidose vial in the immediate patient-treatment area between doses, because proximity improves access without increasing contamination risk."}}
source_row.rationale: CDC safe-injection guidance requires sterile single-use injection equipment and recommends single-patient dedication of multidose vials whenever possible. Option A follows both principles. Option B reuses a needle, which is unsafe even if the syringe is changed. Option C reuses a syringe across patients, which CDC prohibits even if the needle is replaced. Option D places a shared multidose vial in the immediate treatment area, where CDC guidance says it should not be kept for multi-patient use.
source_row.source_detail: CDC Injection Safety — Preventing Unsafe Injection Practices: use a new sterile needle and syringe for every vial entry; dedicate multidose vials to a single patient whenever possible and keep shared vials away from immediate patient-treatment areas. Current CDC injection-safety guidance at cited URL; rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: asepsis, equipment/environmental safety, incident/event prevention and infection-control activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
